options.text: A substance that speeds up a chemical reaction
A substance that changes colour depending on the pH of a solution
A substance that produces gas when added to acid

questions.explanation: An indicator is a substance that changes colour depending on whether it is in an acidic, neutral, or alkaline solution, allowing us to determine the pH.

questions.stem: What colour does litmus turn in an acidic solution?
questions.explanation: Litmus turns red in acidic solutions (pH below 7) and blue in alkaline solutions (pH above 7).

questions.stem: Why is universal indicator more useful than litmus for testing pH?

options.text: Universal indicator shows a range of colours corresponding to different pH values
Universal indicator only works with strong acids
Universal indicator does not change colour

questions.explanation: Universal indicator shows a range of colours (red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple) that correspond to different pH values, while litmus only tells you if a solution is acidic or alkaline.

questions.stem: What colour does universal indicator turn in a neutral solution (pH 7)?
questions.explanation: Universal indicator turns green at pH 7 (neutral). It turns red/orange in strong acids and blue/purple in strong alkalis.

questions.stem: Which indicator is most commonly used in acid-alkali titrations?
questions.explanation: Phenolphthalein and methyl orange are commonly used in titrations because they have a sharp, distinct colour change at a specific pH, making it easy to identify the end point.

questions.stem: Phenolphthalein is colourless in acidic solutions. What colour does it turn in alkaline solutions?
questions.explanation: Phenolphthalein is colourless in acidic and neutral solutions and turns pink in alkaline solutions. This sharp colour change makes it useful for titrations.

questions.stem: Why is universal indicator NOT suitable for use in titrations?

options.text: It changes through many colours gradually, making it hard to identify the exact end point
It does not work with acids

questions.explanation: Universal indicator changes gradually through many colours, making it difficult to identify the precise end point. Titration indicators like phenolphthalein have a sharp, sudden colour change.
